discovery: Quantum cryptography: the invention of quantum key distribution and its realization over global, satellite-based quantum networks

nominees.name: Charles H. Bennett
nominees.affiliation: IBM Thomas J. Watson Research Center, Yorktown Heights, USA

nominees.name: Jian-Wei Pan
nominees.affiliation: University of Science and Technology of China, Hefei, China

motivation: Bennett and Brassard's BB84 protocol (1984) showed that the laws of quantum physics, namely the no-cloning theorem and measurement disturbance, can guarantee secure communication. It founded quantum information science and, with their 1993 teleportation proposal, set the course for quantum networks. Pan Jianwei turned these ideas into physics at unprecedented scales: early multiphoton entanglement and teleportation experiments, then the Micius satellite, which achieved entanglement distribution over 1200 km, ground-to-satellite teleportation and intercontinental quantum key distribution, as well as metropolitan and long-haul quantum networks. Together they took a fundamental insight about quantum measurement and turned it into a working global technology. The 2022 prize recognized tests of entanglement and the 2025 prize recognized macroscopic quantum circuits. The quantum-secure communication that these foundations made possible deserves recognition now.
